findings.quote: Doubting that a body must pass through zero velocity to reverse direction, when in fact any continuous reversal must pass through an instant of rest.
findings.note: Option 3 asserts two things, that (A) is true and that (R) is false, and the entry accounts only for the second. A student who reaches option 3 must also hold the belief that zero velocity forces zero acceleration, which the entry never names.
findings.fix: Believing that zero velocity forces zero acceleration, so treating the assertion as true, and at the same time doubting that a body must pass through zero velocity to reverse direction, when any continuous reversal does pass through an instant of rest.

notes: The assertion is false, since at the top of a vertical throw v = 0 while a = g, and the reason is a true statement, so option 4. The entries for options 1 and 2 each account for both halves of the option they name and are sound.
